channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Live Updates: Protests Spread Across France as Unions Join Student Demonstrations
item.description: The rallies are a test of the strength of the student-led protest movement that has closed hundreds of French high schools since late September.

item.title: NPR: Here are the finalists for the 2026 National Book Awards
item.description: Three-time National Book Award finalist Edwidge Danticat and debut novelist Morgan Thomas are up for the fiction prize. Nonfiction books cover the prison system and music, and queer parenthood.

item.title: BBC News: Watch: At the scene of student protests in Lille
item.description: The BBC's Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from a large demonstration in northern France.

item.title: The Guardian: The west has a blinkered view of African music – and it’s hurting the whole continent’s culture
item.description: The term Afrobeats is applied to all sorts of genres, flattening them into one. Artists, media and the music industry must do better at showing off the richness of African pop In 2024, South African pop star Tyla won the…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Is Europe preparing for a wider war with Russia?
item.description: A British war-game show simulating a Russian attack has drawn a nuclear warning from Moscow.

item.title: Ars Technica: Big Oil asks Supreme Court to kill climate lawsuits before trial
item.description: Oil companies say federal law should block state climate deception claims.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Kevin Roose Didn’t Use AI to Write His Book About AI
item.description: The author of The AGI Chronicles says his book “was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being.”

item.title: WIRED Science: A New Neurotech Startup Launches to Rival Sam Altman’s Merge Labs
item.description: Bridge Neurotech is planning to build a wearable brain-computer interface that uses ultrasound.

item.title: WIRED Business: Mistral Says Its New AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Is the Best Open-Weight Offering Outside of China
item.description: With the release of its new trillion-parameter model, Mistral is hoping to demonstrate it’s “still in the race” to build frontier-level artificial intelligence.

item.title: The New Yorker: Year of the Horse
item.description: After a young tourist was killed in a Central Park carriage accident this summer, the City Council is considering whether to ban horse-drawn carriages forever.

item.description: It’s 5,000 square feet on Gracie Square.
